# improve


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

Ramabana loads a learned folder into every session: `AGENTS.md`, a few
short rules included in every briefing, and skills it opens when a task
calls for them. A round tries to improve that folder from one finished
session, in the manner of the propose, probe and compose step of
Harness². It replays the session’s request `k` times from the commit the
session started at, under the current folder. An editor model reads
those runs and edits a copy of the folder. The request is replayed once
more under the copy. The copy is kept only when that run replied, took a
cheaper route than every base run, and a judge model rated its reply at
least as good as the best base reply. A kept lesson becomes an entry in
the day’s learning file, committed on a `pending/` branch of the
folder’s own git repository, one branch per round.

## Runs

[`replay_clone`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/improve.html#replay_clone)
makes a throwaway clone of the repository at the commit a session
started from. The clone shares no object files with the source and has
no remote, so a replay can neither change nor push to the original.
[`run_turn`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/improve.html#run_turn)
runs one Ramabana turn with no interface, in a fresh config folder, so
no history, extension, skill or project note from the person’s own
config takes part. It reads the turn back from that folder’s history,
which records the request, every tool call and the reply, and leaves
Ramabana’s output in `run.log`. Writes are refused unless `approve`
allows them. A round’s replays pass `read_outside`, so they can read
installed packages and other folders the way an interactive session
does, while their writes stay inside their clone.

from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
with TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    d = Path(d)

    hang.write_text(f'#!/bin/sh\nsleep 30 &\necho $! > {d}/child\nwait\n'); hang.chmod(0o755)
    t = time.time()
    test_fail(lambda: run_turn('x', [d], d/'cfg', exe=str(hang), timeout=1), contains='still going after 1s')
    assert time.time() - t < 10

    time.sleep(0.2)
    test_fail(lambda: os.kill(child, 0), exc=ProcessLookupError)   # the run's own child died with it

## Comparing runs

A route’s cost is a tuple of its route findings, its failed calls and
its calls, and a smaller tuple is a cheaper route. A replay has nobody
to answer approvals, so a refused approval does not count as a failure
and asking again does not count as a `denial_retry`; in a real session a
person would have answered.
[`delivered`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/improve.html#delivered)
says whether a run produced an answer at all: at least one model turn, a
reply, no error, and a `state` of `complete`. A run that was stopped,
abandoned or interrupted has no error, but its reply is cut short.
[`better`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/improve.html#better)
passes a candidate only when it delivered and costs less than every base
run. Tying the best base run is not enough.

A cheaper route alone proves little, because an agent that gives up
early is cheap too. So a round then asks a judge model, through
[`judge_reply`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/improve.html#judge_reply),
to compare every reply, unlabelled and shuffled, and keeps the candidate
only when the judge answers YES: its reply is at least as complete and
correct as the best base reply. The judge also sees the shell commands
each run asked for and was refused, and, when the round has it, what the
person’s own session ran. A run that proposed the command the work
needed is then not marked down for having been refused.

### route_cost

``` python
def route_cost(
    turn
):
```

*`(route findings, failed calls, calls)` for one turn, where refused
approvals and asking again do not count and a smaller tuple is cheaper.*

``` python
def turn(*acts, reply='done'): return {'prompt': 'sizes of the big files', 'reply': reply, 'activity': [dict(tool=t, ok=ok, args=a) for t, ok, a in acts]}
ls, ls2 = ('ls', True, {'path': ''}), ('ls', True, {'path': 'src'})
refused = ('run_shell', False, {'command': 'stat -f %z *.py'})
shell_grep = ('run_shell', True, {'command': 'grep -rn def .'})
base = turn(ls, refused, ls2)
test_eq(route_cost(base), (0, 1, 3))
test_eq(route_cost(turn(shell_grep)), (1, 0, 1))     # a shell grep is a bypass finding
unasked = dict(tool='run_shell', ok=False, args={'command': 'pytest -q'}, detail='Denied by human operator. Reason given: nothing is listening for approvals')
test_eq(route_cost(turn(ls) | {'activity': [dict(tool='ls', ok=True, args={'path': ''}), unasked]}), (0, 0, 2))   # a replay's unanswered approval is not the agent's failure
test_eq(route_cost(turn(ls) | {'activity': [unasked, unasked]}), (0, 0, 2))   # nor is asking again
assert better(turn(ls), [base, turn(ls, ls2)])
assert not better(turn(ls, ls2), [base, turn(ls, ls2)]) # ties the best base run
assert not better(turn(ls, reply=''), [base])
assert not better(turn(reply='claude/sonnet failed (ClaudeError)') | {'usage': {'turns': 0}}, [base])   # no model turn ran: the reply is the failure
assert delivered(turn(ls) | {'usage': '{"turns": 2}'}) and delivered(turn(ls) | {'usage': None})
assert delivered(turn(ls) | {'state': 'complete'}) and not better(turn(ls) | {'state': 'abandoned'}, [base])
for st in ('cancelled', 'abandoned', 'interrupted'): assert not delivered(turn(ls) | {'state': st}), st   # a run cut off, with no error
```

## The learned folder

A candidate folder may hold `AGENTS.md`, skills at
`skills/<name>/SKILL.md` whose frontmatter gives the skill’s `name` and
a `description`, and Dhrona’s dated learning files.
[`check_learned`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/improve.html#check_learned)
lists anything else as a problem, and a round does not run a candidate
that has one. `AGENTS.md` may hold `LEARNED_MAX` characters (2,000). The
dated files are outside that limit. Hidden entries, such as `.git` and
the `.kosha` index Ramabana writes into any folder it opens, are not
part of the folder.

[`keep_lesson`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/improve.html#keep_lesson)
keeps what a round learned as an entry in `dhrona-<date>.md`, one file a
day. An entry holds the request as a heading and the round’s notes, and
no diff.
[`keep_lesson`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/improve.html#keep_lesson)
commits the file on a new `pending/<id>` branch, so a person reviews it
before it reaches HEAD. It does not check the branch out and does not
touch the folder’s branch, index or files, so a person’s uncommitted
edit stays as it was. A batch, a keep and a compaction run whatever the
person has left uncommitted.
[`committed_copy`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/improve.html#committed_copy)
gives each replay the folder’s HEAD, so a replay never sees uncommitted
text.

The dated files have their own limit, `DATED_MAX` (4,000 characters
across all of them). A keep that would pass it raises `ValueError`, and
the round reports the reason in `problems`. Ramabana loads dated files
newest first within its own budget, so the limit only stops unbounded
growth. A dated file whose date is over `DATED_DAYS` (30) days old is
removed by
[`expire_dated`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/improve.html#expire_dated).

[`keep`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/improve.html#keep) commits a
candidate on a new `pending/<id>` branch of the folder’s own repository,
as Dhrona, and leaves the folder’s files alone.
[`keep_lesson`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/improve.html#keep_lesson)
and a compaction use it, and a person accepts the branch with
`ramabana-learned accept <id>`.
[`learned_repo`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/improve.html#learned_repo)
makes the folder a repository the first time and commits what it already
held. In an existing repository it leaves uncommitted changes alone.

Personal details never reach the learned folder or the editor and judge.
[`scrub`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/improve.html#scrub) masks
emails, phone numbers, keys and other identifying values with rahasya,
as numbered labels such as `[EMAIL_1]`. It runs over every evidence
file, the judge’s prompt, the editor’s notes and commit message, and
every file of a candidate before the candidate is run, so what is tested
is what is kept.

### check_learned

``` python
def check_learned(
    folder
):
```

*Problems that rule out a candidate learned folder; empty when it may be
tried.*

``` python
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
with TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    d = Path(d); cand, learned = d/'cand', d/'learned'
    (cand/'skills'/'sizes').mkdir(parents=True)
    (cand/'AGENTS.md').write_text('Read file sizes from `ls`; it reports them.\n')
    (cand/'skills'/'sizes'/'SKILL.md').write_text('---\nname: sizes\ndescription: Compare file sizes.\n---\nUse ls.\n')
    (cand/'.kosha').mkdir(); (cand/'.kosha'/'code.db').write_bytes(b'\x95\x00')   # the index Ramabana writes into a folder it opens
    test_eq(check_learned(cand), [])
    (cand/'notes.txt').write_text('x')
    (cand/'skills'/'bad').mkdir(); (cand/'skills'/'bad'/'SKILL.md').write_text('no frontmatter')
    test_eq(len(check_learned(cand)), 2)
    (cand/'notes.txt').unlink(); shutil.rmtree(cand/'skills'/'bad')
    (learned/'skills'/'stale').mkdir(parents=True); (learned/'skills'/'stale'/'SKILL.md').write_text('old')
    b = keep(cand, learned, 'Read sizes from ls; ask ann@example.com')
    assert b.startswith(PENDING)
    test_eq(sorted(_files(learned)), ['skills/stale/SKILL.md'])   # the working tree, which Ramabana reads, is untouched
    git = lambda *a: _git(learned, *a)
    assert 'skills/stale/SKILL.md' in git('show', '--stat', 'HEAD')   # what was there before Dhrona is the first commit
    test_eq(git('ls-tree', '-r', '--name-only', b).split(), ['AGENTS.md', 'skills/sizes/SKILL.md'])
    test_eq(git('log', '-1', '--format=%an %s', b), 'Dhrona Read sizes from ls; ask [EMAIL_1]')
    test_eq(len(git('worktree', 'list').splitlines()), 1)   # the worktree it committed in is gone
    (learned/'AGENTS.md').write_text('a hand edit')
    assert keep(cand, learned, 'again') != b   # a hand edit does not stop a keep, and the keep leaves it alone
    test_eq((learned/'AGENTS.md').read_text(), 'a hand edit')
    (learned/'AGENTS.md').unlink()
    assert not _uncommitted(learned_repo(d/'empty')) and _git(d/'empty', 'rev-parse', 'HEAD')   # an empty folder gets an empty first commit
    (cand/'AGENTS.md').write_text('Mail ann@example.com or call +1 415 555 0134.\n')
    test_eq(_scrub_folder(cand), ['AGENTS.md'])
    test_eq((cand/'AGENTS.md').read_text(), 'Mail [EMAIL_1] or call [PHONE_1].\n')
```

Ramabana writes a `.kosha` code index into every folder it opens, so one
can sit untracked in the learned folder. Untracked hidden paths are not
a person’s edit, as
[`_files`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/improve.html#_files) and
[`keep`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/improve.html#keep) already
treat them, and
[`learned_repo`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/improve.html#learned_repo)
keeps `.kosha/` out of a new repository’s status. A modified `AGENTS.md`
does not block a batch, a keep or a compaction: Dhrona never stages,
commits or discards a person’s edit.

``` python
with TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    d = Path(d); learned = d/'learned'
    learned.mkdir(); (learned/'AGENTS.md').write_text('Read sizes from `ls`.\n')
    learned_repo(learned)
    (learned/'.kosha').mkdir(); (learned/'.kosha'/'code.db').write_bytes(b'\x95\x00')
    assert '.kosha/' in (learned/'.git'/'info'/'exclude').read_text()
    (learned/'.git'/'info'/'exclude').write_text('')   # a repository made before the exclude line existed
    test_eq(_git(learned, 'status', '--porcelain'), '?? .kosha/')
    test_eq(_uncommitted(learned), False)
    test_eq(learned_repo(learned), learned)
    (learned/'AGENTS.md').write_text('a hand edit')
    test_eq(_uncommitted(learned), True)
    test_eq(learned_repo(learned), learned)   # an edit is not a reason to refuse
    status = _git(learned, 'status', '--porcelain')
status
```

A kept lesson is a short entry in `dhrona-<date>.md`: the request as a
heading and the round’s notes under it, with no diff of the files the
editor changed.
[`keep_lesson`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/improve.html#keep_lesson)
commits that file on a new `pending/<id>` branch off HEAD, in a
temporary worktree. It does not check the branch out, and it does not
touch the learned folder’s checked-out branch, index or files, so a
person’s uncommitted edit stays as it was. A second lesson on the same
day goes on its own branch off the same HEAD. Its file holds both
entries, because it starts from the first branch’s file.

``` python
with TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    d = Path(d); learned = d/'learned'
    learned.mkdir(); (learned/'AGENTS.md').write_text('Read sizes from `ls`.\n')
    learned_repo(learned)
    (learned/'AGENTS.md').write_text('a hand edit\n')   # a person's uncommitted edit
    (learned/'notes.txt').write_text('draft'); _git(learned, 'add', 'notes.txt')   # and a staged file
    state = lambda: (_git(learned, 'rev-parse', 'HEAD'), _git(learned, 'branch', '--show-current'), _git(learned, 'status', '--porcelain'),
                     (learned/'AGENTS.md').read_text(), sorted(_files(learned)))
    before = state()
    entry = lesson_entry('sizes of the big files', 'Read file sizes with `ls`. Ask ann@example.com.')
    b = keep_lesson(learned, entry, 'Lesson from a replay: sizes of the big files')
    assert b.startswith(PENDING)
    test_eq(state(), before)   # branch, index, working tree and HEAD are as they were
    name = f'dhrona-{datetime.now():%Y-%m-%d}.md'
    test_eq(_git(learned, 'diff', '--name-only', 'HEAD', b), name)
    text = _git(learned, 'show', f'{b}:{name}')
    assert 'Read file sizes with `ls`' in text and '[EMAIL_1]' in text and not any(m in text for m in ('@@', '+++', '```diff'))
    b2 = keep_lesson(learned, lesson_entry('a second request', 'Use `ls -l`.'), 'Lesson from a replay: a second request')
    test_eq(_git(learned, 'rev-parse', f'{b2}^'), _git(learned, 'rev-parse', 'HEAD'))
    test_eq(len(_git(learned, 'worktree', 'list').splitlines()), 1)   # no worktree is left behind
    test_eq(state(), before)
    both = _git(learned, 'show', f'{b2}:{name}')
test_eq(both.count('\n## '), 2)
print(both)
```

`LEARNED_MAX` (2,000 characters) counts `AGENTS.md` alone. Dated
learning files have their own cap, `DATED_MAX` (4,000 characters across
all of them).
[`keep_lesson`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/improve.html#keep_lesson)
raises `ValueError` for a lesson that would take the dated files past
it, and a round reports that reason in `problems`. Ramabana loads dated
files newest first within its own budget, so the cap only stops
unbounded growth.

``` python
with TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    d = Path(d); learned = d/'learned'
    learned.mkdir(); (learned/'AGENTS.md').write_text('x' * LEARNED_MAX)
    (learned/'dhrona-2026-01-01.md').write_text('y' * (DATED_MAX - 100))
    test_eq(check_learned(learned), [])   # dated files are outside `LEARNED_MAX`
    (learned/'AGENTS.md').write_text('x' * (LEARNED_MAX + 1))
    test_eq(len(check_learned(learned)), 1)
    (learned/'AGENTS.md').write_text('x' * LEARNED_MAX)
    learned_repo(learned)
    test_fail(lambda: keep_lesson(learned, 'z' * 200, 'Lesson from a replay: long'), contains=f'{DATED_MAX:,}')
    test_eq(_git(learned, 'branch', '--list', 'pending/*'), '')   # a refused lesson leaves no branch
    b = keep_lesson(learned, lesson_entry('short', 'z' * 20), 'Lesson from a replay: short')
    files = _git(learned, 'ls-tree', '--name-only', b)
files
```

## Evidence for the editor

The editor model reads files, not one long prompt.
[`trajectory_md`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/improve.html#trajectory_md)
writes one turn as markdown: the request, each tool call with its
arguments, outcome and shortened result, and the reply.
[`findings_md`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/improve.html#findings_md)
lists each run’s route cost, its findings and its failed or refused
calls. `MISSION` is the editor’s prompt. It says where the evidence and
the candidate folder are, what the editor may change, and that changing
nothing is a valid answer.

### recent_lessons

``` python
def recent_lessons(
    cfg:str='~/.config/ramabana', days:int=30, now:NoneType=None
):
```

*Lessons `remember` recorded in Ramabana’s history in the last `days`
days, newest first, one per lesson text, scrubbed.*

[`recent_lessons`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/improve.html#recent_lessons)
reads the lessons the agent recorded with `remember` from Ramabana’s
history. Every `remember` call is in the history whether the session had
a vault or only a memory file, and shalya’s `parse_lesson` reads the
fields back the same way for both. Only structured lessons count, one
per lesson text, newest first, from the last `days` days, with personal
details scrubbed.
[`lessons_md`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/improve.html#lessons_md)
writes them for the editor as `lessons.md`, tool defects first, because
a tool defect is a candidate for a skill that works around it.

``` python
with TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    cfg = Path(d)
    rem = lambda **a: dict(tool='remember', ok=True, args=a)
    rows = [dict(session='s1', at=time.time() - 40*86400, activity=[rem(text='old lesson', cue='c', component='rule')]),
            dict(session='s2', at=time.time() - 60, activity=[rem(text='a plain note'),
                 rem(text='filter on the root-relative path', cue='empty search', component='tool', evidence='mail ann@example.com said so', confidence='high'),
                 rem(text='bad', component='nonsense'), dict(tool='remember', ok=False, args={'text': 'refused', 'cue': 'x'})]),
            dict(session='s3', at=time.time() - 30, activity=[rem(text='Filter on the  root-relative path', cue='again')])]
    (cfg/'agent-history.jsonl').write_text('\n'.join(map(json.dumps, rows)) + '\n')
    got = recent_lessons(cfg)
    test_eq([(l['lesson'], l['session']) for l in got], [('Filter on the root-relative path', 's3')])   # newest wins; old, plain, invalid and refused are left out
    got = recent_lessons(cfg, now=time.time() - 45)
    test_eq(got[0]['evidence'], 'mail [EMAIL_1] said so')
    md = lessons_md(got + [dict(lesson='keep notes short', component='rule')])
    assert md.index('## Tool defects') < md.index('filter on the root-relative path') < md.index('## Other lessons') and 'ann@' not in md
```

### refused_commands

``` python
def refused_commands(
    turn
):
```

*The shell commands `turn` asked to run and was refused for want of an
approver.*

A replay refuses every shell command, because nobody is there to approve
it, but the command a run asked for still shows what it meant to do.
[`refused_commands`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/improve.html#refused_commands)
lists those commands, and
[`judge_prompt`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/improve.html#judge_prompt)
puts them under that run’s answer, so the judge can count a needed
command, written out for the person to run, as done.
[`ran_commands`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/improve.html#ran_commands)
lists what the person’s own session ran, what failed and what the person
declined, with the reason.
[`judge_prompt`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/improve.html#judge_prompt)
shows these as what the work needed, and the editor reads the same
session as `original.md`.

``` python
def tn(*acts, reply='done'): return {'prompt': 'tidy the drafts', 'reply': reply, 'activity': list(acts)}
look = dict(tool='ls', ok=True, args={'path': ''})
asked = dict(tool='run_shell', ok=False, args={'command': 'git add notes.md && rm draft.md'},
             detail='Denied by human operator. Reason given: nothing is listening for approvals')
broke = dict(tool='run_shell', ok=False, args={'command': 'pytest -q'}, detail='ERROR: exit 1')
ran = dict(tool='run_shell', ok=True, args={'command': 'git add notes.md && rm draft.md'}, detail='(no output)')
nope = dict(tool='run_shell', ok=False, args={'command': 'git push'}, detail='Denied by human operator. Reason given: not yet')
test_eq(refused_commands(tn(look, asked, broke)), ['git add notes.md && rm draft.md'])   # one that ran and failed was not refused
test_eq(ran_commands(tn(look, ran, broke, nope)),
        [('git add notes.md && rm draft.md', 'ran', '(no output)'), ('pytest -q', 'failed', 'ERROR: exit 1'), ('git push', 'declined: not yet', '')])
proposer = tn(look, asked, reply='Run `git add notes.md && rm draft.md`; I could not.')
avoider = tn(look, reply='Done.')
p, label = judge_prompt('tidy the drafts', proposer, [avoider], original=tn(ran))
other = 'B' if label == 'A' else 'A'
blocks = {l: p.split(f'## Answer {l}\n')[1].split('\n## ')[0] for l in 'AB'}
assert 'rm draft.md' in blocks[label] and 'rm draft.md' not in blocks[other], blocks   # under the run that asked for it
assert "person's own session" in p and '(no output)' in p
bare, _ = judge_prompt('tidy the drafts', avoider, [avoider])
assert 'Commands' not in bare and "person's own session" not in bare   # nothing refused and no session: neither section
```

## A round

[`improve_round`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/improve.html#improve_round)
takes a request and the `start` record Ramabana wrote for its session,
`<cfg>/runs/<session>/start.json`, which holds `repo`, `head` and
`dirty`. It raises `ValueError` before any run starts when:

- the start had uncommitted changes, which a replay from `head` would
  not see,
- the learned folder holds files outside the allowed layout,
- `approve` is anything but `ask` or `edits`, so a replay never runs a
  shell command,
- `k` is less than 1.

`work` must be a new folder, or the round raises `FileExistsError`.
Every run, the evidence, the candidate and `report.json` stay in it. If
a base run’s model never answered, the round ends with `base_error`
before the editor runs. If the editor or the candidate run records no
turn or gives no answer, the round ends with that error in the report.
By default replays refuse every write. `approve='edits'` lets them edit
files inside their own clone, which shares no object files with the
source repository. With `learned` set, a kept lesson goes into the day’s
`dhrona-<date>.md` on a `pending/` branch there, and the report names
the branch as `pending`; without it, the round only reports. A lesson
that would take the dated files past `DATED_MAX` characters is not kept,
and the report lists that in `problems`. `lessons`, rows from
[`recent_lessons`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/improve.html#recent_lessons),
go to the editor as `lessons.md`.

The tests below use a stand-in script for `ramabana` that answers each
kind of prompt with a fixed reply. Under it, a run takes one call once
`AGENTS.md` exists and three calls before.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/Karthik777/drona/blob/main/dhrona/improve.py#L383"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### improve_round

``` python
def improve_round(
    prompt, # the request to replay
    start, # `{repo, head, dirty}` from the session's `start.json`
    work, # a new folder for this round's runs, evidence and report
    learned:NoneType=None, # the learned folder whose HEAD the round starts from, and whose `pending/` branch a kept lesson goes onto
    model:NoneType=None, # the model the runs use
    editor:NoneType=None, # the model that edits the candidate
    k:int=2, # base runs
    approve:str='ask', # `edits` lets a replay edit files inside its throwaway clone
    exe:str='ramabana',
    read_outside:bool=True, # replays read outside their clone, as a session started with `--read-outside` does
    original:NoneType=None, # the person's own turn for this request; the editor and the judge see what its commands did
    lessons:tuple=(), # `recent_lessons` rows the editor reads as evidence
    timeout:int=1800, # seconds before a replay, base or candidate, is abandoned
    limit:int=8, # dollars the round's recorded runs may cost before it stops
):
```

*Run one round of `k` base runs, one edit to the learned folder, one run
under the edit and the decision, and return the report.*

*Dollars the runs in round folder `work` recorded, whether or not the
round finished; a run that recorded no turn adds nothing.*

``` python
FAKE = r'''#!/usr/bin/env python3
"A stand-in for `ramabana`: the editor writes AGENTS.md; a run takes one call once AGENTS.md exists, three before."
import json, sys
from pathlib import Path
a = sys.argv[1:]
roots, cfg, prompt = a[a.index('--root') + 1].split(','), Path(a[a.index('--cfg') + 1]), a[-1]
(cfg/'argv.json').write_text(json.dumps(a))
ls = dict(tool='ls', ok=True, args={'path': ''})
if prompt.startswith('You improve'):
    Path(roots[0], 'AGENTS.md').write_text('Read file sizes from ls.\n')
    acts, reply = [dict(tool='create_file', ok=True, args={})], 'base-1 call 1: wrote AGENTS.md'
elif prompt.startswith('A person asked'): acts, reply = [], 'YES\nIt names the same file and size.'
elif (cfg/'learned'/'AGENTS.md').exists(): acts, reply = [ls], 'big.py 50'
else: acts, reply = [ls, dict(tool='run_shell', ok=False, args={'command': 'stat big.py'}), ls], 'big.py 50'
(cfg/'agent-history.jsonl').write_text(json.dumps(dict(prompt=prompt, activity=acts, reply=reply, usage={'cost': 0})) + '\n')
'''
with TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    d = Path(d)
    exe, repo = d/'fake-ramabana', d/'repo'
    exe.write_text(FAKE); exe.chmod(0o755); repo.mkdir()
    def git(*a): return subprocess.run(['git', '-C', str(repo), *a], check=True, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
    git('init', '-q'); (repo/'big.py').write_text('x = 1\n'); git('add', '.')
    git('-c', 'user.name=t', '-c', 'user.email=t@example.com', 'commit', '-qm', 'one')
    start = dict(repo=str(repo), head=git('rev-parse', 'HEAD'), dirty=[])
    r = improve_round('sizes of the big files', start, d/'work', learned=d/'learned', exe=str(exe))
    test_eq((r['bases'][0]['route'], r['candidate']['route'], r['adopted']), ((0, 1, 3), (0, 0, 1), True))
    assert r['judge'].startswith('YES')
    assert not (d/'work'/'base-1'/'repo').exists(), 'a checkout goes once its run ends'
    clone = replay_clone(start, d/'clone')
    test_eq(subprocess.run(['git', '-C', str(clone), 'remote'], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout, '')   # nothing can push back
    test_eq((clone/'big.py').read_text(), 'x = 1\n')
    test_eq(sorted(_files(d/'learned')), [])   # kept as pending: HEAD, which Ramabana reads, is unchanged
    dated = f'dhrona-{datetime.now():%Y-%m-%d}.md'
    test_eq(_git(d/'learned', 'ls-tree', '-r', '--name-only', r['pending']), dated)
    assert 'wrote AGENTS.md' in _git(d/'learned', 'show', f"{r['pending']}:{dated}")   # the editor's notes, not a diff
    test_eq(sorted(_files(d/'work'/'candidate')), ['AGENTS.md'])   # the runs sit beside the candidate, never in it
    assert (d/'work'/'report.json').exists()
    assert not (d/'work'/'evidence'/'original.md').exists()
    real = dict(prompt='sizes of the big files', reply='big.py 50', activity=[dict(tool='run_shell', ok=True, args={'command': 'stat -f %z big.py'}, detail='50')])
    r = improve_round('sizes of the big files', start, d/'w7', exe=str(exe), original=real)
    assert 'stat -f %z big.py' in (d/'w7'/'evidence'/'original.md').read_text()   # the editor reads what the person's session ran
    test_fail(lambda: improve_round('x', start, d/'work', exe=str(exe)), contains='exists')
    test_fail(lambda: improve_round('x', start | dict(dirty=['big.py']), d/'w2', exe=str(exe)), contains='uncommitted')
    test_fail(lambda: improve_round('x', start, d/'w3', approve='auto', exe=str(exe)), contains='approve')
    doubting = d/'doubting-ramabana'
    doubting.write_text(FAKE.replace("'YES\\nIt names", "'NO\\nIt asks instead of naming")); doubting.chmod(0o755)
    r = improve_round('sizes of the big files', start, d/'w5', learned=d/'learned-5', exe=str(doubting))
    test_eq((r['candidate']['route'], r['adopted']), ((0, 0, 1), False))   # a cheaper route that answers worse is not kept
    assert r['judge'].startswith('NO') and not (d/'learned-5').exists()
    mute = d/'mute-ramabana'
    mute.write_text(FAKE.replace("'YES\\nIt names the same file and size.'", "''")); mute.chmod(0o755)
    r = improve_round('sizes of the big files', start, d/'w6', exe=str(mute))
    assert 'no answer' in r['judge_error'] and not r['adopted']
    assert all(map(_says_yes, ['YES', '**YES**', 'yes: it names the file'])) and not any(map(_says_yes, ['YESTERDAY', 'NO', 'Answer C: YES']))
    dead = d/'dead-ramabana'
    dead.write_text(FAKE.replace("usage={'cost': 0}", "usage={'turns': 0}")); dead.chmod(0o755)
    r = improve_round('sizes of the big files', start, d/'w4', exe=str(dead))
    assert 'no answer' in r['base_error'] and 'big.py 50' in r['base_error'] and not (d/'w4'/'editor').exists()   # no editor runs on empty evidence
    paid = d/'paid-ramabana'
    paid.write_text(FAKE.replace("usage={'cost': 0}", "usage={'cost': 1}")); paid.chmod(0o755)   # each run records a dollar
    r = improve_round('sizes of the big files', start, d/'w8', exe=str(paid), limit=1.5)
    assert '$2.00' in r['cost_limit'] and len(r['bases']) == 2 and not r['adopted'] and not (d/'w8'/'editor').exists()   # the bases passed the limit: no editor runs
    for name, room in [('base-1', '1.50'), ('base-2', '0.50')]:
        argv = json.loads((d/'w8'/name/'cfg'/'argv.json').read_text())
        test_eq(argv[argv.index('--max-cost') + 1], room)
    r = improve_round('sizes of the big files', start, d/'w9', exe=str(paid), limit=3.5)
    assert 'candidate' in r and 'judge' not in r and 'cost_limit' in r and not r['adopted']   # the candidate run passed it: no judge runs
    r = improve_round('sizes of the big files', start, d/'w10', exe=str(paid))
    test_eq((r['adopted'], 'cost_limit' in r, ROUND_LIMIT), (True, False, 8))   # a round of $5 is under the default
    for name, room in [('base-1', '8.00'), ('base-2', '7.00'), ('editor', '6.00'), ('candidate-run', '5.00'), ('judge', '4.00')]:
        argv = json.loads((d/'w10'/name/'cfg'/'argv.json').read_text())
        test_eq(argv[argv.index('--max-cost') + 1], room)
    r = improve_round('sizes of the big files', start, d/'w12', exe=str(paid), limit=1.2)
    assert len(r['bases']) == 1 and not (d/'w12'/'base-2').exists() and not (d/'w12'/'editor').exists(), r   # $0.20 left starts no run: `--max-cost` cannot stop a Claude Code run in time
    assert 'less than the $0.25 a run needs' in r['cost_limit'] and not r['adopted']
    r = improve_round('sizes of the big files', start, d/'w13', exe=str(paid), limit=0.1)
    assert r['bases'] == [] and not (d/'w13'/'base-1').exists() and 'cost_limit' in r   # a night with $0.10 left runs nothing
    full = d/'learned-full'; full.mkdir(); (full/'dhrona-2026-01-01.md').write_text('y' * DATED_MAX); learned_repo(full)
    r = improve_round('sizes of the big files', start, d/'w11', learned=full, exe=str(paid))
    assert not r['adopted'] and 'pending' not in r and f'past the {DATED_MAX:,}' in r['problems'][0], r   # the cap's reason is in the report
```

A turn passes its dollar allowance to Ramabana only when one is
supplied; the command receives two decimal places.

``` python
with TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    d = Path(d)
    exe = d/'fake-ramabana'
    exe.write_text(FAKE); exe.chmod(0o755)
    cost_turn = run_turn('sizes', [d], d/'uncapped', exe=str(exe))

## Training on past sessions

Older sessions have no `start.json`, so they record no starting commit,
and most record no folder either.
[`session_start`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/improve.html#session_start)
works both out. It places a turn in the repository that most of its
absolute tool paths fall in, or else the first git repository among
`roots`. Its `head` is that repository’s last commit before the turn’s
`at`, which may be epoch seconds or an ISO date; an unreadable `at`
leaves the turn unplaced. `dirty` is None because nobody knows what was
uncommitted at that time.

[`trainable`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/improve.html#trainable)
picks the turns worth replaying. It takes the first turn of each session
when the request is at least 40 characters long, carried no attachments,
ended complete and without an error, made between 1 and `max_calls`
calls, and cost something, meaning at least one finding or failed call.
An attached file belonged only to that session, so a replay could not
see it. It also drops a turn that made a commit, because `at` marks the
end of the turn and the commit found for its start would already contain
that commit. A request asked in several sessions is kept once, from the
cheapest, and the result is ordered by number of calls, fewest first.
[`trainable_sessions`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/improve.html#trainable_sessions)
runs
[`trainable`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/improve.html#trainable)
over Ramabana’s own history and session index, takes each session’s
start from its `start.json` entry for the repository the work used, and
drops a session whose entry had uncommitted changes. The entry is
matched on the resolved path, because Ramabana writes resolved paths and
a tool call may name a path through a link. An unreadable `start.json`
or session index, such as one a crash cut short, counts as missing.

href="https://github.com/Karthik777/drona/blob/main/dhrona/improve.py#L522"

*The person’s request inside `<user-request>` tags, else the whole

``` python
import os
from datetime import datetime, timezone
with TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    repo = Path(d)/'repo'; repo.mkdir()
    def git(*a, when=None):
        env = os.environ | ({'GIT_AUTHOR_DATE': when, 'GIT_COMMITTER_DATE': when} if when else {})
        return subprocess.run(['git', '-C', str(repo), *a], check=True, capture_output=True, text=True, env=env).stdout.strip()
    git('init', '-q')
    for n, when in [(1, '2026-01-01T00:00:00Z'), (2, '2026-03-01T00:00:00Z')]:
        (repo/'a.py').write_text(f'x = {n}\n'); git('add', '.')
        git('-c', 'user.name=t', '-c', 'user.email=t@example.com', 'commit', '-qm', f'c{n}', when=when)
    january = git('rev-list', '--max-parents=0', 'HEAD')
    t = {'session': 's1', 'at': datetime(2026, 2, 1, tzinfo=timezone.utc).timestamp(), 'model': 'claude-opus-5-5',
         'prompt': '<user-request>\nwhere is x defined, and which files read it? list them\n</user-request>',
         'activity': [dict(tool='grep', ok=True, args={'pattern': 'x', 'path': str(repo/'a.py')}),
                      dict(tool='run_shell', ok=False, args={'command': 'cat a.py'})]}
    test_eq((session_start(t)['repo'], session_start(t)['head']), (str(repo), january))   # the last commit before the turn
    test_eq(session_start(t | {'at': '2026-02-01T00:00:00+00:00'})['head'], january)        # an ISO `at` reads the same
    test_eq((session_start(t | {'activity': []}), session_start(t | {'at': None}), _toplevel('relative/dir')), (None, None, None))
    test_eq(session_start(t | {'activity': []}, roots=[str(repo)])['repo'], str(repo))
    attached = t | {'session': 's3', 'prompt': '<user-request>\nwhat does this screenshot show about the layout?\n</user-request>\n<attachments>\nimage /tmp/paste.png\n</attachments>'}
    cheaper = t | {'session': 's5', 'activity': [dict(tool='grep', ok=False, args={'pattern': 'x', 'path': str(repo/'a.py')})]}
    committed = t | {'session': 's6', 'prompt': 'where is x defined, and who imports it? list each file please',
                     'activity': t['activity'] + [dict(tool='git_commit', ok=True, args={'message': 'm'})]}
    got = trainable([t, t | {'prompt': 'a later turn in the same session'}, t | {'session': 's2', 'prompt': 'ok'},
                     t | {'session': 's4'}, attached, cheaper, committed])
    test_eq([(s['session'], s['prompt'], s['model']) for s in got], [('s5', 'where is x defined, and which files read it? list them', 'claude-opus-5-5')])
    test_eq(got[0]['turn']['session'], 's5')   # the session's own first turn, for the editor and the judge
    # s4 and s5 ask what s1 asked and s5 costs least; s3 names a file only its session had; s6's start would hold its own commit
    cfg = Path(d)/'cfg'; (cfg/'runs'/'s1').mkdir(parents=True)
    (cfg/'agent-history.jsonl').write_text(json.dumps(t) + '\n')
    rec = [dict(repo='/elsewhere', head='abc', dirty=[]), dict(folder=str(repo), repo=str(repo), head=january, dirty=[])]
    (cfg/'runs'/'s1'/'start.json').write_text(json.dumps(rec))
    test_eq([(s['start']['head'], s['start']['inferred']) for s in trainable_sessions(cfg)], [(january, False)])   # the entry for the repository the work used
    rec[1]['dirty'] = ['a.py']; (cfg/'runs'/'s1'/'start.json').write_text(json.dumps(rec))
    test_eq(trainable_sessions(cfg), [])
```

``` python
import time
with TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    d = Path(d); repo = d/'repo'; repo.mkdir()
    def git(*a): return subprocess.run(['git', '-C', str(repo), *a], check=True, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
    git('init', '-q'); (repo/'a.py').write_text('x = 1\n'); git('add', '.')
    git('-c', 'user.name=t', '-c', 'user.email=t@example.com', 'commit', '-qm', 'c')
    (link := d/'link').symlink_to(repo)
    t = {'session': 's1', 'at': time.time() + 60, 'model': 'm', 'prompt': 'where is x defined, and which files read it? list them',
         'activity': [dict(tool='grep', ok=True, args={'path': str(link/'a.py')}), dict(tool='run_shell', ok=False, args={'command': 'cat a.py'})]}
    test_eq(trainable([t | {'state': 'cancelled'}]), [])   # a turn the person stopped seeds nothing
    test_eq(len(trainable([t | {'state': 'complete'}])), 1)
    cfg = d/'cfg'; (cfg/'runs'/'s1').mkdir(parents=True); (cfg/'agent-history.jsonl').write_text(json.dumps(t) + '\n')
    rec = dict(folder=str(repo), repo=str(repo.resolve()), head=git('rev-parse', 'HEAD'), dirty=['a.py'])   # Ramabana resolves the path
    (cfg/'runs'/'s1'/'start.json').write_text(json.dumps([rec]))
    test_eq(trainable_sessions(cfg), [])   # the record for the work's repository, reached through a link, says it began dirty
    for bad in ('[{"repo', '{}', 'null', '[1]'):
        (cfg/'runs'/'s1'/'start.json').write_text(bad)
        test_eq([s['start']['inferred'] for s in trainable_sessions(cfg)], [True])   # an unreadable record is no record
    (cfg/'agent-sessions.json').write_text('{"sess')
    test_eq(len(trainable_sessions(cfg)), 1)
```

## Batches

[`improve_batch`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/improve.html#improve_batch)
runs
[`improve_round`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/improve.html#improve_round)
on up to `n` sessions in turn, in the order
[`trainable_sessions`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/improve.html#trainable_sessions)
gives. Every round starts from the learned folder’s HEAD, so uncommitted
text of a person’s never reaches a replay. Each kept lesson waits on its
own `pending/` branch, so each can be accepted or rejected alone. With
`cfg` set, the batch first expires what went `days` days unused
([`expire_learned`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/improve.html#expire_learned),
listed in `expired.json`) and gives every round the lessons of the last
`days` days
([`recent_lessons`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/improve.html#recent_lessons)).
With `compact_at` set, it then proposes a compaction of `AGENTS.md` when
the file is over that fraction of `LEARNED_MAX` (see Compaction), and
writes the result to `compaction.json`. `models` keeps the sessions
recorded with those models, and `skip` leaves sessions out by id. A
round that fails, for example because its model cannot start or its
repository is gone, becomes a row with `error`, and the batch goes on.
`summary.json` in `work` holds every row so far, and `[]` when no
session matched. An `approve` other than `ask` or `edits` raises before
any round runs. Uncommitted files in the learned folder never stop a
batch.

Each row has a `cost`: the dollars recorded by every run in the round’s
folder
([`round_cost`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/improve.html#round_cost)),
meaning the base runs, the editor, the candidate and the judge, whether
or not the round finished. A run killed at its timeout, or one whose
model reports no cost, adds nothing. With `budget` set, no new round
starts once the rounds so far have cost that much, so a batch can
overshoot its budget by the cost of its last round. A batch with a
learned folder holds
[`learned_lock`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/improve.html#learned_lock)
on it for its whole run, and a second batch on the same folder, from the
command line or a scheduled beat, raises `RuntimeError` before it
creates anything. The lock is a file beside the folder, and the
operating system releases it when the batch’s process ends, even in a
crash. `dhrona-improve` runs a batch from the command line. It requires
a learned folder, and prints one line per round, with the pending
branches and `REVIEW`, which says to review them with `/learned` in
Ramabana or `ramabana-learned` in a shell.

### expire_dated

``` python
def expire_dated(
    learned, days:int=30, now:NoneType=None
):
```

*Remove each committed dated learning file whose date is over `days`
days old, one commit per file as Dhrona; returns the names. Only that
file’s path is staged or committed, so other edits stay as they are.*

[`expire_learned`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/improve.html#expire_learned)
removes what Dhrona proposed and a person accepted once it has gone
`days` days without use or renewal, and commits the removal so
`git revert` brings it back. A skill counts as used when a session read
it with `read_skill` or the turn loaded it, and renewed when a later
accepted round changed it. `AGENTS.md` is in every briefing, so a
paragraph there counts only as renewed when an accepted round last
changed one of its lines; a fenced block is never split. Only commits
whose message starts with `LESSON` can expire: what was there before
Dhrona, and anything a person committed, stays. When nobody worked in
the last `days` days, nothing expires, because nothing had the chance to
be used. While the folder has uncommitted changes, skills and
`AGENTS.md` paragraphs do not expire, because the removal is committed
with the files it changed and must not stage a person’s edit. It stages
and commits only the paths it changed.

[`expire_dated`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/improve.html#expire_dated)
removes each committed dated learning file over `DATED_DAYS` (30) days
old, by the date in its name. It runs `git rm` and a commit on that one
path as Dhrona, one commit a file, and touches no other path. It works
on a folder with uncommitted edits.
[`expire_learned`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/improve.html#expire_learned)
calls it first, so a dated file expires even when nobody worked.

``` python
with TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    d = Path(d); cfg, learned, cand = d/'cfg', d/'learned', d/'cand'
    (learned/'skills'/'mine').mkdir(parents=True); (learned/'skills'/'mine'/'SKILL.md').write_text('---\nname: mine\ndescription: x\n---\nhand\n')
    (learned/'AGENTS.md').write_text('A rule a person wrote.\n')
    learned_repo(learned)
    old = str(int(time.time()) - 40*86400)
    def lesson(files, msg, when):
        for rel, text in files.items(): (learned/rel).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True); (learned/rel).write_text(text)
        env = os.environ | {'GIT_COMMITTER_DATE': when, 'GIT_AUTHOR_DATE': when}
        subprocess.run(['git', '-C', str(learned), 'add', '-A'], check=True)
        subprocess.run(['git', '-C', str(learned), *_AS_DHRONA, 'commit', '-qm', msg], check=True, env=env)
    lesson({'skills/stale/SKILL.md': '---\nname: stale\ndescription: x\n---\nold\n', 'skills/read/SKILL.md': '---\nname: read\ndescription: x\n---\nold\n',
            'AGENTS.md': 'A rule a person wrote.\n\nAn old rule.\n```\ncode\n\nmore\n```\n'}, f'{LESSON}: old', old)
    lesson({'AGENTS.md': 'A rule a person wrote.\n\nAn old rule.\n```\ncode\n\nmore\n```\n\nA new rule.\n'}, f'{LESSON}: new', str(int(time.time())))
    cfg.mkdir()
    test_eq(expire_learned(learned, cfg), [])   # no session in the window: nothing had the chance to be used
    (cfg/'agent-history.jsonl').write_text(json.dumps(dict(session='s', at=time.time(), activity=[dict(tool='read_skill', ok=True, args={'name': 'read'})])) + '\n')
    gone = expire_learned(learned, cfg)
    test_eq(gone, ['skills/stale', 'AGENTS.md: An old rule.'])
    test_eq((learned/'AGENTS.md').read_text(), 'A rule a person wrote.\n\nA new rule.\n')
    test_eq(sorted(p.name for p in (learned/'skills').iterdir()), ['mine', 'read'])
    assert not _uncommitted(learned) and 'Expired after 30 days' in _git(learned, 'log', '-1', '--format=%s')
```

[`expire_learned`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/improve.html#expire_learned)
also removes each dated learning file whose date is over `DATED_DAYS`
(30) days old
([`expire_dated`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/improve.html#expire_dated)).
It removes the file with `git rm` and commits that path alone as Dhrona,
one commit a file. It stages and commits no other path, so it runs on a
folder with uncommitted edits. A person’s edit to a dated file that is
not yet committed keeps the file.

``` python
with TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    d = Path(d); learned = d/'learned'
    learned.mkdir(); (learned/'AGENTS.md').write_text('Read sizes from `ls`.\n')
    (learned/'dhrona-2026-08-01.md').write_text('# Dhrona lessons 2026-08-01\n'); (learned/'dhrona-2026-10-20.md').write_text('# Dhrona lessons 2026-10-20\n')
    learned_repo(learned)
    (learned/'AGENTS.md').write_text('a hand edit\n')
    (learned/'notes.txt').write_text('draft'); _git(learned, 'add', 'notes.txt')   # a person's staged file
    before = _git(learned, 'status', '--porcelain')
    gone = expire_learned(learned, d/'cfg', now=datetime(2026, 10, 26).timestamp())
    test_eq(gone, ['dhrona-2026-08-01.md'])
    test_eq(_git(learned, 'show', '--name-only', '--format=%an', 'HEAD'), 'Dhrona\n\ndhrona-2026-08-01.md')   # one path, authored by Dhrona
    test_eq(_git(learned, 'status', '--porcelain'), before)   # the edit is still unstaged, the staged file still staged
    test_eq((learned/'AGENTS.md').read_text(), 'a hand edit\n')
    test_eq(sorted(_files(learned)), ['AGENTS.md', 'dhrona-2026-10-20.md', 'notes.txt'])
before
```

## Compaction

Accepted lessons add up, and `ramabana-learned accept` refuses one that
would take `AGENTS.md` past `LEARNED_MAX`.
[`compact_learned`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/improve.html#compact_learned)
proposes a shorter file. git blame splits HEAD’s `AGENTS.md` into
paragraphs Dhrona proposed, where every line came from a commit whose
message starts with `LESSON` or `COMPACT`, and the rest, which a person
wrote or which was there before Dhrona. The editor model rewrites only
Dhrona’s paragraphs. It merges lessons that overlap, drops duplicates
and lessons a later one replaced, and keeps fenced code blocks whole,
aiming at `target` characters (`COMPACT_TARGET`, 1,200) for the whole
file. A person’s paragraph stands in the file as a marker line such as
`[kept 1]`, with its text given separately for context, and the marker
becomes the original paragraph again, byte for byte. The prompt and the
rewrite are scrubbed.

A rewrite is refused, and nothing is committed, when it drops, moves,
repeats or edits a marker, drops a fenced block, is no shorter than the
file it started from, or passes `LEARNED_MAX`. One that passes waits on
a `pending/` branch like a kept candidate, so a person reviews it with
`ramabana-learned`. Its commit message starts with `COMPACT`, so what it
wrote counts as Dhrona’s own: it expires as a lesson does, and a later
compaction may rewrite it. Accepting it does not renew the lessons it
rewrote. Each rewritten paragraph takes the newest time of the lessons
it draws on, matched by shared words, or of all of them when none
matches, and the commit’s `TIMES` trailer records that time for each of
its lines.
[`_blame`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/improve.html#_blame) reads
the trailer, so a paragraph merged from two stale lessons expires on
their schedule, not 30 days after the accept.

`onto` folds in a pending candidate that `ramabana-learned accept`
refused for size. The file that candidate would make is compacted, the
compaction holds the candidate’s other files too, and its `INCLUDES`
trailer names the candidate, so accepting the compaction accepts the
candidate and drops its branch. Ramabana’s
[`accept`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/rounds.html#accept) then
moves every other pending candidate onto the new HEAD where it applies
cleanly, and marks the rest stale.

[`compact_learned`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/improve.html#compact_learned)
takes
[`learned_lock`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/improve.html#learned_lock).
It refuses while a batch runs, when `AGENTS.md` holds no paragraph
Dhrona proposed, and when a compaction is already pending. Uncommitted
changes in the folder do not stop it: it works from HEAD and leaves the
working tree alone. It returns `{ok, pending, before, after, cost}`,
where `before` and `after` are character counts and `cost` the editor’s
dollars, or `{ok: False, error}`. The editor runs as the judge does: one
headless Ramabana turn with the `editor` model, in an empty folder. A
test passes `chat`, a function from prompt to reply.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/Karthik777/drona/blob/main/dhrona/improve.py#L834"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### compact_learned

``` python
def compact_learned(
    learned, # the learned folder
    target:int=1200, # characters to aim the whole `AGENTS.md` at
    chat:NoneType=None, # a function from prompt to reply; None asks `editor` in one headless Ramabana turn
    editor:NoneType=None, # the model that rewrites; Ramabana's routing default when None
    exe:NoneType=None, # the Ramabana command; the one beside this Python when None
    onto:NoneType=None, # a pending id to fold in: the file it would make is compacted, and accepting the compaction accepts it too
):
```

*Propose a shorter `AGENTS.md` for `learned` on a `pending/` branch:
`{ok, pending, before, after, cost}`, or `{ok: False, error}`.*

### compaction_prompt

``` python
def compaction_prompt(
    before, paras, target:int=1200
):
```

*The scrubbed prompt asking the editor to compact `before`, whose
`paras` come from
[`_paragraphs`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/improve.html#_paragraphs),
with a person’s paragraphs as `[kept N]`.*

``` python
with TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    learned = Path(d)/'learned'; learned.mkdir()
    def commit(text, msg, who=_AS_DHRONA):
        (learned/'AGENTS.md').write_text(text); _git(learned, 'add', '-A'); _git(learned, *who, 'commit', '-qm', msg)
    head = '# Rules\n\nA rule a person wrote. Mail bob.ray@example.com.\n'
    (learned/'AGENTS.md').write_text(head); learned_repo(learned)
    tests = 'Run the tests with:\n```\nuv run pytest -q\n```'
    lessons = [f'Lesson {i}: read file sizes with ls -l, not stat. ' + 'Say it again. ' * 12 for i in range(6)] + [tests]
    text = head
    for l in lessons: text += f'\n{l}\n'; commit(text, f'{LESSON}: {l[:9]}')
    commit(text + '\nA closing rule a person wrote.\n', 'by hand', ('-c', 'user.name=t', '-c', 'user.email=t@x'))
    before = (learned/'AGENTS.md').read_text()
    paras = _paragraphs(learned)
    test_eq([mine for _, mine, _ in paras], [False, False, *[True] * 7, False])
    sent = []
    def chat(reply):
        def f(prompt): sent.append(prompt); return reply
        return f
    good = f'[kept 1]\n\n[kept 2]\n\nRead file sizes with ls -l, not stat. Ask ann.lee@example.com.\n\n{tests}\n\n[kept 3]'
    r = compact_learned(learned, chat=chat(f'```markdown\n{good}\n```'))   # one fence around the whole reply is unwrapped
    assert r['ok'], r
    out = subprocess.run(['git', '-C', str(learned), 'show', f"{r['pending']}:AGENTS.md"], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
    assert out.startswith(head) and out.endswith('\n\nA closing rule a person wrote.\n')   # a person's paragraphs, byte for byte
    assert tests in out and '[EMAIL_1]' in out and 'ann.lee' not in out   # the fence whole, the rewrite scrubbed
    test_eq((r['before'], r['after']), (len(before), len(out)))
    assert r['after'] < COMPACT_TARGET and (learned/'AGENTS.md').read_text() == before   # HEAD waits for review
    assert 'bob.ray' not in sent[0] and '[kept 3]' in sent[0] and 'Lesson 5' in sent[0]   # the prompt is scrubbed
    subj = _git(learned, 'log', '-1', '--format=%s', r['pending'])
    test_eq(subj, f'{COMPACT} ({len(before):,} → {len(out):,} characters)')
    assert 'already pending' in compact_learned(learned, chat=chat(good))['error']
    _git(learned, *_AS_DHRONA, 'cherry-pick', r['pending'])   # what `ramabana-learned accept` does
    test_eq([mine for _, mine, _ in _paragraphs(learned)], [False, False, True, True, False])   # the compaction is Dhrona's own, so it expires as a lesson does
    _git(learned, 'branch', '-D', r['pending'])
    text = (learned/'AGENTS.md').read_text()
    commit(text + '\n' + 'Another lesson. ' * 20 + '\n', f'{LESSON}: more')
    nothing = lambda: test_eq(_git(learned, 'branch', '--list', 'pending/*'), '')
    def refused(reply, why):
        assert why in (e := compact_learned(learned, chat=chat(reply))['error']), e
        nothing()
    refused('[kept 1]\n\n[kept 2]\n\nShort.\n\n[kept 3]', 'fenced block')
    refused(f'[kept 1]\n\n[kept 2]\n\n{tests}\n\n' + 'Longer. ' * 300 + '\n\n[kept 3]', 'no shorter')
    refused(f'[kept 1]\n\nA rule a person rewrote.\n\n{tests}\n\n[kept 3]', 'a person wrote')
    refused(f'[kept 1]\n\n[kept 2]\nand more\n\n{tests}\n\n[kept 3]', 'a person wrote')
    refused(f'[kept 2]\n\n[kept 1]\n\n{tests}\n\n[kept 3]', 'a person wrote')
    refused('', 'no file')
    with learned_lock(learned): refused(good, 'batch is running')
    (learned/'AGENTS.md').write_text('an uncommitted edit\n')
    r = compact_learned(learned, chat=chat(good))   # an edit does not stop a compaction, which works from HEAD
    assert r['ok'], r
    test_eq((learned/'AGENTS.md').read_text(), 'an uncommitted edit\n')
    _git(learned, 'branch', '-D', r['pending']); _git(learned, 'checkout', '-q', '--', '.')
    plain = Path(d)/'plain'; plain.mkdir(); (plain/'AGENTS.md').write_text('Only a person wrote this.\nAnd this, right after.\n'); learned_repo(plain)
    assert 'nothing Dhrona proposed' in compact_learned(plain, chat=chat('x'))['error']
```

``` python
with TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    d = Path(d); learned, cfg = d/'learned', d/'cfg'; learned.mkdir(); cfg.mkdir()
    (learned/'AGENTS.md').write_text('A rule a person wrote.\n'); learned_repo(learned)
    old, text = str(int(time.time()) - 40*86400), 'A rule a person wrote.\n'
    def lesson(add, when=None, msg=f'{LESSON}: x'):
        global text
        text += f'\n{add}\n'; (learned/'AGENTS.md').write_text(text)
        env = os.environ | ({'GIT_COMMITTER_DATE': when, 'GIT_AUTHOR_DATE': when} if when else {})
        subprocess.run(['git', '-C', str(learned), 'add', '-A'], check=True)
        subprocess.run(['git', '-C', str(learned), *_AS_DHRONA, 'commit', '-qm', msg], check=True, env=env)
    lesson('Read file sizes with ls -l, never stat. ' * 8, old)
    lesson('Prefer listing directories with ls before reading files. ' * 8, old)
    lesson('Search code with rg, keeping globs narrow. ' * 8)
    chat = lambda p: '[kept 1]\n\nRead file sizes with ls -l, never stat; list directories with ls before reading files.\n\nSearch code with rg, keeping globs narrow.'
    chat.cost = 0.25
    r = compact_learned(learned, chat=chat)
    test_eq((r['ok'], r['cost']), (True, 0.25))
    assert TIMES in _git(learned, 'log', '-1', '--format=%B', r['pending'])
    _git(learned, *_AS_DHRONA, 'cherry-pick', r['pending']); _git(learned, 'branch', '-D', r['pending'])   # accepted today
    (cfg/'agent-history.jsonl').write_text(json.dumps(dict(session='s', at=time.time(), activity=[])) + '\n')
    gone = expire_learned(learned, cfg)
    test_eq(len(gone), 1); assert gone[0].startswith('AGENTS.md: Read file sizes')   # merged from two 40-day-old lessons: it expires by them, not by the accept
    test_eq((learned/'AGENTS.md').read_text(), 'A rule a person wrote.\n\nSearch code with rg, keeping globs narrow.\n')
    a = d/'cand'; shutil.copytree(learned, a, ignore=_HIDDEN)
    (a/'AGENTS.md').write_text((learned/'AGENTS.md').read_text() + '\n' + 'Run tests with pytest -q before any commit. ' * 45 + '\n')
    (a/'skills'/'sizes').mkdir(parents=True); (a/'skills'/'sizes'/'SKILL.md').write_text('---\nname: sizes\ndescription: x\n---\nuse ls\n')
    big = '20261019-084007-bcbc13'   # an id `scrub` would mask as a card number
    _git(learned, 'branch', '-m', keep(a, learned, f'{LESSON}: tests'), PENDING + big)
    assert len(_show(learned, PENDING + big)) > LEARNED_MAX   # too long to accept
    assert 'nothing is pending' in compact_learned(learned, chat=chat, onto='20990101-000000-abcdef')['error']
    r = compact_learned(learned, chat=lambda p: '[kept 1]\n\nSearch code with rg, keeping globs narrow.\n\nRun tests with pytest -q before any commit.', onto=big)
    assert r['ok'] and r['before'] > LEARNED_MAX and r['after'] < COMPACT_TARGET, r
    body = _git(learned, 'log', '-1', '--format=%B', r['pending'])
    assert body.startswith(f'{COMPACT} with {big} (') and f'{INCLUDES}{big}' in body
    test_eq(_git(learned, 'ls-tree', '-r', '--name-only', r['pending']), 'AGENTS.md\nskills/sizes/SKILL.md')   # the candidate's skill comes too
    test_eq(_git(learned, 'diff', '--name-only', 'HEAD', r['pending']), 'AGENTS.md\nskills/sizes/SKILL.md')   # one commit off HEAD, so accepting it is one pick
```

## History health

Ramabana’s history is a log nobody reads until it is 224 MB.
[`history_health`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/improve.html#history_health)
makes one streaming pass over it, one line at a time, and reports its
size, the rows and bytes of each day, the largest row, and the groups of
failing tool calls. A group is a tool plus the first 60 characters of an
`ERROR` result, or of a `TypeError` about a missing positional argument,
counted over the last `days` and over the `days` before. A `defect` is a
tool that crashed, a `habit` is the model or the guard disagreeing about
how to use a tool, and `noise` is a shell command that exited non-zero.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/Karthik777/drona/blob/main/dhrona/improve.py#L879"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### history_health

``` python
def history_health(
    cfg:str='~/.config/ramabana', # Ramabana's config folder, whose `agent-history.jsonl` is read
    days:int=14, # the window; the `days` before it give each group's `previous` count
    now:NoneType=None, # epoch seconds; the present when None
    top:int=20, # groups to return, most frequent first
    fixed:NoneType=None, # `load_fixed` rows: a group's occurrences at or before its fix time are not counted
):
```

*One streaming pass over `cfg`’s history: log size, rows and bytes per
day, the largest row, failing-call groups, guard refusals, repeated
calls and sub-agent results without a `state:` line.*

A night’s note gets a line for each threshold the report crosses: a log
over `LOG_MAX_MB` or growing over `LOG_GROWTH_MB` a day for a week, a
row over `ROW_MAX_MB`, and a defect group seen more than `DEFECT_MAX`
times or twice as often as in the window before. Each such defect also
gets an issue draft in the night’s folder, with its count and trend,
three example sessions, one raw error and the tool. A habit is never an
issue: past `DEFECT_MAX` it becomes a candidate lesson, which a person
reviews before anything is learned.

A defect a person has fixed goes in the fixed-defects record, `FIXED`
(`~/.config/dhrona/fixed.json`, moved by `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`), keyed by
the slug that names its issue draft. Each entry holds `at`, when the fix
was made, a `note` such as a commit or a version, and an optional
`check`.
[`record_fix`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/improve.html#record_fix)
writes an entry, and `dhrona-fixed SLUG --note NOTE --check CHECK` does
the same from a shell.
[`history_health`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/improve.html#history_health)
counts only the occurrences after `at`. A defect with any occurrence
after `at` is reported as `recurred after fix`, whatever its count, and
its issue draft says so. A defect with none is not reported and gets no
draft.

A `check` is a shell command or a `module:callable` path. A shell
command passes on exit 0. A callable passes when it returns without
raising and does not return `False`. A check that runs longer than 60
seconds fails. Before each night’s batch,
[`nightly`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/improve.html#nightly)
runs every recorded check once
([`check_lines`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/improve.html#check_lines))
and puts each failure in the note as `fix check failed for SLUG`.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/Karthik777/drona/blob/main/dhrona/improve.py#L1013"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

``` python
with TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    d = Path(d); now = 1_700_000_000.
    ex = [dict(session=f's{n}', at=now - n*3600) for n in (1, 2, 3, 4)]
    def grp(tool, key, kind, count, previous): return dict(tool=tool, key=key, kind=kind, count=count, previous=previous, examples=ex[:3], raw=f'{key} in full')
    h = dict(now=now, days=14, log_bytes=250*10**6, largest=dict(bytes=6*10**6, session='big', at=now),
             per_day={f'2023-11-{n:02d}': dict(rows=9, bytes=30*10**6) for n in range(7, 15)},
             groups=[grp('grep', 'TypeError: grep() missing 1 required positional argument', 'defect', 21, 0), grp('ls', 'TypeError: ls() missing 1 required positional argument', 'defect', 4, 2),
                     grp('stat', 'TypeError: stat() missing 1 required positional argument', 'defect', 5, 0), grp('view_file', 'ERROR: Unsafe path', 'habit', 50, 40)])
    lines, defects = health_findings(h)
    test_eq([g['tool'] for g in defects], ['grep', 'ls'])   # over the limit, and doubled; five a fortnight is neither
    assert len(lines) == 5 and 'MB' in lines[0] and 'a day' in lines[1] and 'big' in lines[2] and lines[3].startswith('defect grep')
    quiet = h | dict(log_bytes=10, largest=dict(bytes=1, session='x', at=now), per_day={}, groups=h['groups'][2:3])
    test_eq(health_findings(quiet), ([], []))
    paths = issue_drafts(defects, d/'night')
    test_eq(sorted(p.parent.name for p in paths), ['issues', 'issues'])
    text = paths[0].read_text()
    assert 'grep' in text and '21' in text and 's1' in text and 's3' in text and 's4' not in text and 'missing 1 required positional argument in full' in text
    assert '2023-11-14' in text   # an example's timestamp
    cand = lesson_candidates(h, d/'night')
    assert 'view_file' in cand.read_text() and 'TypeError' not in cand.read_text()
text
```

``` python
with TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    d = Path(d); now, day = 1_700_000_000., 86400
    def row(ago, sid, *acts): return dict(session=sid, at=now - ago*day, activity=list(acts))
    def call(tool, detail, ok=False, **args): return dict(tool=tool, ok=ok, args=args, detail=detail)
    miss = "TypeError: code_tools.<locals>.grep() missing 1 required positional argument: 'pattern'"
    rows = [row(1, 's1', call('grep', miss)), row(2, 's2', call('grep', miss)), row(3, 's3', call('grep', miss)), row(20, 's0', call('grep', miss)),
            row(1, 's4', call('run_shell', 'ERROR: exit 1', command='a'), call('run_shell', 'ERROR: exit 2', command='b')),
            row(1, 's5', call('run_shell', '`| tail` cuts the output a failure is in. Run the command bare', command='ls | tail')),
            row(1, 's6', call('ls', 'a', True, path='.'), call('ls', 'a', True, path='.'), call('ls', 'a', True, path='/etc')),
            row(1, 's7', call('delegate_search', 'found it\nstate: completed', True, q='a'), call('delegate_search', 'found nothing', True, q='b')),
            row(1, 's8', call('view_file', 'ERROR: Unsafe path /etc/passwd is outside the open folders', path='/etc/passwd')),
            row(1, 'big', call('ls', 'x'*3000, True))]
    (d/'agent-history.jsonl').write_text('\n'.join(map(json.dumps, rows)) + '\nnot json\n')
    h = history_health(d, days=14, now=now)
    g = {(x['tool'], x['kind']): x for x in h['groups']}
    test_eq((g['grep', 'defect']['count'], g['grep', 'defect']['previous']), (3, 1))
    test_eq(sorted(e['session'] for e in g['grep', 'defect']['examples']), ['s1', 's2', 's3'])
    test_eq(g['grep', 'defect']['raw'], miss)
    test_eq([x['kind'] for x in h['groups'] if x['tool'] == 'run_shell'], ['noise', 'noise'])
    test_eq(g['view_file', 'habit']['count'], 1)
    test_eq((h['guard_refusals'], h['repeats'], h['no_state']), (1, 1, 1))
    test_eq((h['log_bytes'], h['largest']['session']), ((d/'agent-history.jsonl').stat().st_size, 'big'))
    assert h['largest']['bytes'] > 3000 and sum(v['rows'] for v in h['per_day'].values()) == len(rows)
    test_fail(lambda: history_health(d/'nowhere'), exc=FileNotFoundError)
    # examples name distinct sessions, so one session failing three times does not fill every slot

    test_eq([e['session'] for e in history_health(d, days=14, now=now)['groups'][0]['examples']], ['sA', 'sB'])

## Efficiency

A round asks whether a lesson makes one answer better. The efficiency
check asks what the turns cost. A turn’s cost grows with its tool calls,
because each call sends the whole context to the model again.
[`efficiency_of`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/improve.html#efficiency_of)
reads history rows and counts, per turn: tool calls, input tokens, and
the habits that add calls without adding work.
[`efficiency_findings`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/improve.html#efficiency_findings)
gives a night’s note one line for each threshold that the counts cross.

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 50%" />
<col style="width: 50%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>count</th>
<th>what it finds</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>calls_per_turn</code></td>
<td>turns past <code>EFF_CALLS</code> tool calls on average</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>shell_search</code></td>
<td>shell calls that only search or list files</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>redirects</code></td>
<td>shell output written to <code>/tmp</code> files and read back</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>sleeps</code></td>
<td>shell calls that sleep to wait for background work</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>test_reruns</code></td>
<td>the same test command run again with no edit between</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>memory_writes</code>, <code>memory_reads</code></td>
<td>notes written much more often than they are read</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

A habit is reported when it occurs more than `EFF_HABIT` times in the
last `EFF_DAYS` days.
[`efficiency`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/improve.html#efficiency)
reads those days from Ramabana’s history.

href="https://github.com/Karthik777/drona/blob/main/dhrona/improve.py#L1072"

### efficiency_of

``` python
def efficiency_of(
    rows
):
```

*Tool calls, input tokens and wasteful habits over history `rows`, one
turn per `turn_id` with its last row counting.*

``` python
now = 1_700_000_000.
def turn(tid, calls, inp=0): return dict(turn_id=tid, session='s', at=now, usage=dict(input=inp), activity=calls)
def sh(cmd): return dict(tool='run_shell', args=dict(command=cmd), ok=True)
slow = [sh('grep -n x a.py'), sh('pytest -q > /tmp/o.out 2> /tmp/o.err'), sh('pytest -q > /tmp/o.out 2> /tmp/o.err'), sh('sleep 60')]
rows = [turn('t1', [], 1),   # a turn's earlier row: the last row of a turn id is the one that counts
        turn('t1', slow + [dict(tool='view_file', args={}, ok=True)] * 40, 5_000_000),
        turn('t2', [dict(tool='remember', args={}, ok=True)] * 12 + [dict(tool='memory_search', args={}, ok=True)] * 2, 1_000_000)]
e = efficiency_of(rows)
test_eq((e['turns'], e['calls'], e['shell'], e['shell_search'], e['redirects'], e['sleeps'], e['test_reruns'], e['memory_writes'], e['memory_reads']),
        (2, 58, 4, 1, 2, 1, 1, 12, 2))
test_eq(e['input_per_turn'], 3_000_000)
lines = efficiency_findings(e, calls=20, habit=0)
test_eq(len(lines), 6)   # calls per turn, shell searches, redirects, sleeps, test reruns, memory writes
test_eq(efficiency_findings(efficiency_of([turn('t3', [sh('pytest -q')])])), [])
```

A fix is recorded once and counted from its time. In the history below,
`grep` fails three times before the fix and once after it. Without the
record the group counts four. With it the group counts the one failure
after `at`, and
[`health_findings`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/improve.html#health_findings)
reports it as `recurred after fix`, although one is far below
`DEFECT_MAX`. A fix made after the last failure leaves no group.

``` python
with TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    d = Path(d)
    hist = [row(ago, f's{ago}', call('grep', miss)) for ago in (5, 4, 3, 1)]   # days ago; the fix is 2 days ago
    (d/'agent-history.jsonl').write_text('\n'.join(map(json.dumps, hist)) + '\n')
    slug = _slug(dict(tool='grep', key=miss[:60]))
    test_eq(history_health(d, now=now)['groups'][0]['count'], 4)
    path = d/'fixed.json'
    entry = record_fix(slug, note='0.1.19', at=_iso(now - 2*day), path=path)
    test_eq(load_fixed(path), {slug: entry})
    h = history_health(d, now=now, fixed=load_fixed(path))
    g, = h['groups']
    test_eq((g['count'], g['fixed']['note']), (1, '0.1.19'))   # the three failures before the fix are not counted
    lines, defects = health_findings(h)
    test_eq(len(defects), 1)
    assert 'recurred after fix (0.1.19' in lines[0], lines
    assert 'recurred after fix' in issue_drafts(defects, d/'night')[0].read_text()
    test_eq(history_health(d, now=now, fixed={slug: dict(at=_iso(now - day/2))})['groups'], [])   # a fix after the last failure leaves nothing to report
    test_fail(lambda: record_fix(slug, at='soon', path=path), contains='fix time')
    test_eq(check_lines({'ok': dict(check='true'), 'py': dict(check='platform:system'), 'none': dict(note='no check')}), [])
    bad = check_lines({'b': dict(check='exit 3', note='v1'), 'c': dict(check='json:nothing')})
    assert bad[0].startswith('fix check failed for b (v1): exit 3') and 'AttributeError' in bad[1], bad
bad
```

## Every night

[`nightly`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/improve.html#nightly) is
the function a scheduled beat calls. `ramabana-tick` finds it through
the `ramabana.ticks` entry point named `dhrona`, and calls it when the
pobblebonk schedule named `dhrona` fires, passing the schedule’s payload
as `fire`. The payload must hold a positive `budget` in dollars, or
[`nightly`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/improve.html#nightly)
raises `ValueError` before any round runs. A `timeout` that is not a
positive number, given as a number or as text, raises the same way. The
other keys are optional:

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 33%" />
<col style="width: 33%" />
<col style="width: 33%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>key</th>
<th>meaning</th>
<th>default</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>n</code></td>
<td>rounds</td>
<td>3</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>k</code></td>
<td>base runs per round</td>
<td>2</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>model</code></td>
<td>the model the replays use</td>
<td>each session’s own</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>editor</code></td>
<td>the model that edits and judges</td>
<td>Ramabana’s default</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>models</code></td>
<td>a list of model ids whose sessions are kept</td>
<td>all</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>max_calls</code></td>
<td>the most calls a replayed turn may have made</td>
<td>40</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>cfg</code></td>
<td>the Ramabana config folder</td>
<td><code>~/.config/ramabana</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>learned</code></td>
<td>the learned folder</td>
<td><code>&lt;cfg&gt;/learned</code>, the folder Ramabana loads</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>work</code></td>
<td>where batch folders go</td>
<td><code>NIGHTLY</code>, <code>~/.cache/dhrona/nightly</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>expire_days</code></td>
<td>days of history the lessons come from, and that a proposed skill or
rule may go unused before it expires</td>
<td>30</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>compact_at</code></td>
<td>the fraction of <code>LEARNED_MAX</code> past which
<code>AGENTS.md</code> gets a compaction proposed</td>
<td>0.8</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>timeout</code></td>
<td>seconds before a replay, base or candidate, is abandoned; its batch
row then carries
<code>the run in ... was still going after Ns</code></td>
<td>1800</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>exe</code></td>
<td>the Ramabana command</td>
<td>see below</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>fixed</code></td>
<td>the fixed-defects record (see History health)</td>
<td><code>FIXED</code>, <code>~/.config/dhrona/fixed.json</code></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

Each night writes a new batch folder under `work`, named by the time it
started. It skips every session that a batch under `work` has already
started a round on
([`tried_sessions`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/improve.html#tried_sessions)),
including rounds that failed, and when no session is left it creates
nothing. A night with no session left still expires what went unused.
[`nightly`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/improve.html#nightly)
returns the note the beat leaves for the next session: how many rounds
ran, the pending branches waiting for review, what expired, each
recorded fix check that failed, a compaction it proposed, and the
dollars spent against the budget.

After expiry and before the rounds, a night proposes a compaction when
`AGENTS.md` is over `compact_at` of `LEARNED_MAX`, holds a paragraph
Dhrona proposed, and has no compaction pending. The note says
`compaction pending <branch>`, or why none was proposed. A night tries
one compaction per HEAD: the HEAD it tried is kept in a file beside the
learned folder, so a compaction a person rejected is not proposed again
until HEAD moves. The editor’s turn counts against `budget`: its cost is
in the night’s total, in the note’s compaction line and in
`compaction.json`, and a compaction that spends the budget leaves no
round to run.

The note names each failed round with the first line of its error
([`night_error`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/improve.html#night_error)).
Where Ramabana’s error suggests `/model NAME`, which only an interactive
session can act on, the note names the schedule key to set instead:
`model` when the replay’s own model could not run, `editor` otherwise.
An error saying Claude Code is not logged in, as happens when a job
started by launchd cannot read the login from the keychain, gets a line
saying to run `claude /login` or to put `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in
Ramabana’s `beat.env`, which bills the API instead of the subscription.

A night where every round failed and nothing was spent could not run at
all: a missing tool, a model that does not start, a lost login. It
writes the note into a `night-failed` file in its batch folder and
raises
[`NightFailed`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/improve.html#nightfailed)
with the note as its message, so pobblebonk retries the fire and, after
the last try, leaves the note as `gave up after N tries`.
[`tried_sessions`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/improve.html#tried_sessions)
does not count a session from such a night until it has sat in
`FAILED_TRIES` (2) of them, so the retry replays the same sessions and a
session that never runs is eventually passed over. A night with no
session left, or with one round that ran, returns its note and is not
retried.

If a batch is already running on the learned folder, the night returns a
note saying so and runs nothing. pobblebonk 0.0.4 and later renew a
running fire’s claim, so this only happens when a second beat starts
while one is still running. Any other failure raises, and pobblebonk
retries a fire that raised, up to the schedule’s `retries`. Add the
schedule with `retries=2` and `retry_after='1h'`, so a night that could
not run gets one more try an hour later (pobblebonk 0.0.5; an older
pobblebonk retries after 30 seconds instead):

``` python
from ramabana.monitor import pob
pob().add('dhrona', cron='0 3 * * *', retries=2, retry_after='1h', budget=20, n=3)
```

An existing schedule takes the same change with
`pob().update('dhrona', retries=2, retry_after='1h')`. Each try runs
replays under `timeout`, and the beat that runs them stops itself after
`ramabana-tick --limit`, so a night cannot hold the beat forever.

Without `exe`, a night runs the `ramabana` installed beside the Python
that runs the beat, or else the one found on `PATH`. This matters
because a beat started by cron or launchd has a short `PATH`.

    past = dict(session='s1', model='m1', at=time.time() + 60, reply='big.py 50',
                prompt='<user-request>\nWhat are the sizes of the big files in this repository?\n</user-request>',
                activity=[ls, dict(tool='run_shell', ok=False, args={'command': 'stat big.py'}), ls])
    (cfg/'agent-history.jsonl').write_text(json.dumps(past) + '\n')
    fire = AttrDict(budget=5, cfg=str(cfg), work=str(d/'nights'), exe=str(exe))

    assert 'ramabana-learned list' not in note, 'the CLI takes `--cmd list`, so a bare `list` fails'
    assert not sorted(_files(cfg/'learned')) and 'pending/' in _git(cfg/'learned', 'branch', '--list', 'pending/*')   # waiting for review
    test_eq(tried_sessions(d/'nights'), {'s1'})
    test_eq(nightly(fire), 'no session left that an earlier night has not tried')
    test_eq(len(list((d/'nights').iterdir())), 1)   # the second night created no folder
    test_fail(lambda: nightly(AttrDict(cfg=str(cfg))), contains='budget')
    for bad in (0, -5, 'soon'): test_fail(lambda: nightly(AttrDict(fire, timeout=bad)), contains='timeout')
    test_eq(nightly(AttrDict(fire, timeout='900')), 'no session left that an earlier night has not tried')   # a payload may hold the number as text
    fixed = d/'fixed.json'
    record_fix('grep-missing', note='0.1.19', check='exit 3', path=fixed); record_fix('ls-missing', check='true', path=fixed)
    note = nightly(AttrDict(fire, fixed=str(fixed)))
    assert 'fix check failed for grep-missing (0.1.19): exit 3' in note and 'ls-missing' not in note, note   # a failing quick check is in the night's note, a passing one is not

    time.sleep(1.1)   # batch folders are named to the second
    test_fail(lambda: nightly(fire), exc=NightFailed)
    test_eq(tried_sessions(d/'nights'), {'s1'})   # passed over after FAILED_TRIES such nights
    test_eq(nightly(fire), 'no session left that an earlier night has not tried')

A night that refuses to start is as visible as one whose rounds all
failed. The batch folder and its `night-failed` marker exist before any
check that can raise, `summary.json` holds the error, and
[`nightly`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/improve.html#nightly)
returns a note naming the refusal. A refusal is not retried by raising,
because a retry would meet the same refusal. Uncommitted files in the
learned folder are not a refusal.

with TemporaryDirectory() as d:

    def git(*a): return subprocess.run(['git', '-C', str(repo), *a], check=True, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
